validated_results.reason: Original case-control analysis reporting adjusted odds ratios for prostate cancer according to measured salivary melatonin rhythm amplitude, a human biomarker of the requested exposure.

extraction.comparison_type: high vs low melatonin amplitude (median of controls cutoff)
extraction.population: Men with prostate cancer cases and controls from the CAPLIFE study

sample_size.location: abstract, methods; total_n derived from reported group counts 40 + 41 = 81

cases.excerpt: A total of 40 PCa cases and 41 controls from the CAPLIFE study were analyzed to determine the salivary melatonin rhythm through 6 saliva samples.

effect_size.excerpt: A high amplitude was associated with a decreased risk of PCa, aOR=0.31 (95% CI 0.11, 0.86), while a late acrophase could be increased risk of PCa, aOR=2.36 (95% CI 0.88, 6.27). Patients with PCa always had lower melatonin levels than men without PCa, independent of urinary symptomatology or extension and aggressiveness of the tumor.
